question_text: How does the characteristic affect perception in the person here — and record no effect if none is evidenced.

distinct_answers.text: Impairs in the disordered register — Psa 36:2: hatred-avoidance distorts self-perception; group 1199's mas.te.mah destroys prophetic perception entirely. Enables and sharpens in the righteous register — righteous hatred sharpens perception of moral reality (Psa 119:104).
Impairs — contempt filters out the actual worth of the despised object. It produces a systematically distorted perception: what has been designated as worthless cannot be perceived as it actually is.

Impairs in the inverted form (group 252-002 — abhorring justice means perceiving righteousness as the repugnant thing). Enables in the righteous form — sharpening the perception of what is genuinely morally repugnant.
Impairs — the cruel person's perception fails to register the suffering of others as morally significant. The perceptive faculty's mercy-triggering function is absent.

Distorts — reproach reorganises perception of the self (as worthless) and of the social environment (as threatening further reproach). The person under sustained reproach perceives threat where there may be none.
Sharpens — the adversary relationship demands heightened perceptive vigilance (1Pe 5:8).
Inverts — malice reorganises perception so that another's suffering triggers pleasure rather than compassion. The perceptive faculty is operating but in a systematically inverted direction.
[Sub-group not separately addressed in source — see cluster-level finding (cluster_subgroup_id IS NULL) for this prompt]

Deepens — love opens the cognitive access to the inner world of the beloved (Joh 15:15 — Group 1553: friendship constituted by knowledge-disclosure). Love enables a form of perception that strangers cannot access.

Triggers — compassion is triggered by perception and in turn deepens the comforter's perceptive sensitivity to suffering (2Cor 1:4 — Group 602 parallel: the one who has been comforted in affliction perceives others' affliction more acutely).
[Sub-group not separately addressed in source — see cluster-level finding for this prompt]
Deepens — the person who has been comforted in affliction perceives others' distress more precisely. The suffering-and-comfort pathway sharpens the perception of suffering in others.

**[CLUSTER]** E. Righteousness enables and deepens perception: uprightness in B produces the capacity to understand "every good path" (Pro 2:9); the righteous person in A2 is one who can discern (A2-011: the thoughts of the righteous are just, Pro 12:5); the reckoning faculty in F is sharpened through right use (sustained weighing of suffering against glory, Rom 8:18). Wickedness impairs perception: the wicked do not know how to do right (Amo 3:10); none of the wicked shall understand (Dan 12:10). The pattern is consistent: righteousness is perceptually enabling; wickedness is perceptually disabling.

Both: wisdom includes perceptive capacity (VCG08 understanding Scripture) and produces perceptive outcomes (the wise person sees what others miss). Wisdom is a wisdom-for-perceiving-rightly, not raw perception.
M15-B IS a form of perception. Bin, suniēmi name the perceptive act itself. Understanding does not produce perception as a secondary outcome — it is the perceptive act.
Both: ya.da names the act of knowing (perception as act) and the state of having known (knowledge as possession). The characteristic is perception-as-act and perception-as-product simultaneously.
M15-D IS constitutively perceptive. Sa.khal, diakrinō, ta.am all name the discriminating perceptive act.
M15-E uses perception as input but is itself a volitional-deliberative act, not a perceptive one.
M15-F uses received perception as its material but is itself a dwelling activity, not a new perceptive act.
M15-G is the content produced by perception — the outcome, not the activity.
M15-H is a revelatory instrument — it produces perception (or reveals its absence) but is not itself a perceptive faculty.
Not applicable to BOUNDARY as mechanisms rather than characteristics.
Impairs — anxiety dulls alertness to what is coming (Luk 21:34: hearts weighed down → day comes suddenly).

Complicates — distazō is not a failure to perceive but a failure to move from perception to trust. The perceptive faculty is functioning; the doubt is the failure to complete the movement from seeing to believing.

Enables: Job 33:26 (795-002) — the graced-accepted person "sees his face"; grace opens the perceptive access to God's presence. The grace-reception opens sight to what was previously inaccessible. Luk 2:40 (888-003) — Jesus "filled with wisdom and the favour of God was upon him" — grace and wisdom together deepen the perceptive-cognitive capacity.
Enables: ya.tav as "seeing well" (Jer 1:12) suggests goodness deepens the accuracy of perception — the good person sees rightly. No impairment pattern evidenced in M39-B.
Impairs: inner closure systematically impairs perception. Isa 6:10 (cannot see, hear, understand), Rev 3:17 (not realising), Job 12:5 (contempt without genuine perception of misfortune).

Distorts: insatiability distorts perception by keeping the perceptual faculty in permanent unsatisfied motion — the never-satisfied eye is always engaged but never resting. The deceitfulness of riches bypasses accurate perception, substituting a false impression.

Redirects: Moses's perception is not impaired but redirected — from Egypt's visible treasure to the invisible reward. This is a different mode of perceptual engagement: the faculty functions but its object is changed.

M01-A reverential fear **enables and deepens** perception in the ordered direction. Pro 2:5 ("fear of the Lord is the fruit of earnest seeking after wisdom — an inner understanding arrived at through diligent pursuit") implies that fear sharpens spiritual discernment. Psa 25:14 (fear positions the person to receive God's friendship and knowledge of his covenant — covenant knowledge opened by fear-posture). Fear of God appears to enable a kind of receptive attentiveness to God's communication.

Acute fear (M01-B), terror-as-force (M01-C), and dismay (M01-D) routinely **impair** the perceptive faculty: Isa 21:3 (dismay so overwhelming the prophet "cannot see"); Job 32:15 (friends dismayed into speechlessness — the verbal-perceptive loop shut down); Dan 5:6 (color change and limb-failure as perceptive-system overwhelm); Mat 14:26 (disciples mis-perceive Jesus as a ghost — fear distorting perceptive identification). M01-D-VCG-03 is the most explicit: dismay systematically shuts down perception and speech.

M01-E somatic trembling — where it is the response to theophany — does not impair but rather **registers** divine reality through the body. The E-VCG-02 trembling-at-word tradition may **deepen** receptive perception: Ezr 9:4; 10:3 (those who tremble at God's word gather for covenant action — the trembling marks a community whose perceptive attentiveness to God's word is heightened).

The perceptive faculty is: **enabled/deepened** by M01-A reverential fear; **bypassed** by the involuntary character of M01-B's theophanic fear (the disciples cannot choose not to fear the risen Jesus); **impaired** by M01-D dismay (systematic shutdown) and by M01-B's distorting social-fear (Isa 8:12: social fear "distorts perception of true danger"). The pattern suggests that ordered fear (M01-A) enhances perception while disordered fear (M01-B's social register, M01-C, M01-D) impairs it.

Anger impairs perception. Isa 42:25 (M02-B-VCG-06): when God's rage is poured out on Israel in battle, "the people failed to perceive or take it to heart — the inner faculty of understanding is closed off." The rage impairs the perceptive capacity of those under it — they cannot read what is happening to them. Pro 27:4 (M02-E-VCG-04) describes jealousy as irresistible and overwhelming — implying it overrides the moderating functions of perception and discernment.

Job 36:18 (M02-B-VCG-03) shows rage as "inward enticement — it can seduce a person into scoffing" — the rage distorts moral perception rather than enabling it. The filling, possessing form of anger bypasses moral perceptive capacity and substitutes its own driven energy.

Grief deepens moral perception. The conscience-driven sighing of Eze 9:4 (M03-E-VCG-01) shows grief as the sign of active inner perception — those who sigh and groan over wickedness are those whose moral perceptive faculty is functioning correctly. Prophetic grief arises from prophetic perception (Elisha weeping after foreknowledge — 2Ki 8:11 — M03-A-VCG-04; Jer 9:1 — M03-A-VCG-04). In this sense, grief can be an indicator that perception is functioning: the one who perceives the weight of sin, loss, and catastrophe genuinely will grieve. Grief does not bypass or impair perception; it is often the evidence that perception is operating.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Exultation deepens perception: Psa 40:16 and 70:4 show that those who "seek" God rejoice in him — the seeking (a perceptive-seeking act) enables exultation, which in turn sustains the seeking. The inverted passages show impairment: exultation directed at idols (Hos 10:5) is accompanied by spiritual blindness (the idol will depart; the joy will become mourning). Rightly-directed exultation appears to sharpen perception of God's reality; misdirected exultation blinds.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Joy deepens perception in its rightly-directed form: Psa 107:42 ("the upright see it and are glad") — joy at God's acts reinforces the attentiveness to divine action that produced it; Psa 126:3 ("the Lord has done great things for us; we are glad") — the glad perception of divine acts sustains the orientation toward God. Joy impairs perception in its misdirected form: Mat 13:20 (joy without root fails when testing comes — the initial perceptive joy was accurate but too shallow); Act 12:14 (Rhoda's overwhelming joy at Peter's voice means she fails to perceive his actual presence at the gate — joy can momentarily overwhelm practical perception). The rocky-ground passages (Mat 13:20; Luk 8:13) show Joy without depth actually preventing sustained engagement with reality.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Suffering-Joy deepens spiritual perception: 1Pe 1:8 (belief in the unseen Christ producing inexpressible joy) shows that Spirit-enabled Suffering-Joy opens the person to perceive realities that ordinary sensory perception cannot access. It does not bypass natural-world perception (the suffering is genuinely perceived and felt) but adds a second perceptive layer — the Spirit-enabled perception of eschatological reality that recontextualises the natural-world suffering.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Gladness deepens perception in its healthy form: the person who habitually evaluates rightly (M04-L-VCG-02) develops the perceptive capacity to see what is genuinely good or not-good in moral and relational situations. Misdirected Gladness impairs perception: Num 14:3 (fear distorting the perceptive evaluation of the land); Isa 39:8 (Hezekiah's self-referential perception missing the full implication of Isaiah's word). Accurate Gladness both requires and trains accurate perception.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Delight both deepens and can distort perception: (1) **Deepens**: Psa 111:2 ("great are the works of the Lord, studied by all who delight in them") — Delight in God's works drives sustained perceptive engagement; the person who delights in God's law reads and re-reads with increasing attention (Psa 1:2); (2) **Distorts**: Rev 13:3 (the marveling at the beast) — corrupt Delight produces a captivated perception that cannot see the beast's true nature; Isa 58:2 (delight to seek God without moral reality) — surface perceptive-religious engagement masking the absence of genuine inner Delight; Jer 6:10 (the closed ear taking no pleasure) — blocked Delight correlates with impaired perception.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Genuine Pleasure deepens perception: the person who genuinely tastes God's goodness (Psa 34:8) perceives him more accurately; Psa 27:4's gaze upon God's beauty is perceptive engagement of the highest kind. Distorted Pleasure impairs perception: Pro 9:17 (stolen bread appearing pleasant — deceived perception evaluating the wrong object as pleasant); the ni.cho.ach withheld (Lev 26:31) implies the covenant-unfaithful person's worship-perception is distorted, offering what cannot reach God.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Wonder deepens perception: Psa 119:18's "open my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of your law" shows that divine opening of perception enables Wonder; Psa 119:27's "make me understand… and I will meditate on your wondrous works" shows that Wonder-capacity grows with understanding. Wonder also depends on perception — its failure (Neh 9:17 — "not mindful") is a failure to perceive or register what has been seen. Wonder-failure is perceptive failure.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The consistent pattern: rightly-directed characteristics deepen perception; misdirected characteristics distort or bypass it. (1) **Deepens**: Wonder (Char 6) — "open my eyes, that I may behold" — Wonder expands and deepens perceptive capacity; Delight (Char 4) — Psa 111:2 (delight in God's works drives sustained study); Joy (Char 2) — sustained joy at God's acts reinforces attentiveness to divine action; (2) **Distorts/bypasses**: Delight misdirected (Rev 13:3 — captivated perception that cannot see the beast's true nature); Joy without root (Mat 13:20 — initial accurate perception of goodness but too shallow to sustain); Wonder misapplied (Rev 17:6 — marvelling at the harlot); (3) **Unique pattern in Suffering-Joy (Char 7)**: deepens specifically the spiritual-perceptive faculty — enabling perception of what is not visible (1Pe 1:8). This is a form of perception-deepening unique in the cluster: not sharpening sensory perception but opening the inner being to eschatological realities not accessible through sensory channels.

**[CHAR-1]** E — In its acute form, shame **impairs** perception by collapsing the upward gaze: the face that cannot be lifted, the eyes that turn away. The shamed person cannot look clearly at what is before them — shame produces a kind of perceptive closing-down. However, in the M07-C corrective mode, shame **sharpens** perception: being shown the temple's design produces shame, and shame then becomes the condition for receiving clearer spiritual perception (Eze 43:10-11). Corrective shame is thus a perception-clearing event: shame removes the blindness of false confidence and opens the person to see what is actually required.

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 primarily impairs perception by collapsing the upward gaze: the humiliated are "dismayed and confounded." The haughty eyes targeted in Isa 5:15 and Psa 18:27 show the perceptive faculty as the site of prideful distortion. In the VCG-03 divine-abasement mode, CHAR-2 can be read as perception-correcting: the proud are forced to see what they actually are.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — CHAR-3 is produced by failed perception — the judge who does not see the worth of persons (Luk 18:2/4); dishonoring God through hypocrisy while not perceiving the self-contradiction (Rom 2:23). CHAR-3 impairs the relational-perceptive faculty in the dishonorer.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 engages moral perception — the conscience that recognises "certain deeds done in secret are so morally degraded that even speaking of them is shameful" (Eph 5:12) is exercising moral-perceptive discernment. The inverted conscience (VCG-03) shows distorted moral perception: what should be seen as shameful is seen as honourable.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — Perception is engaged in CHAR-5 through the contempt-er's misperception of worth (they do not see the genuine worth of the person they despise) and through the recipient's perception of their own contempt-received condition. Psa 14:6 — "shame the plans of the poor" — shows how contempt targets the poor person's inner plans and confidence (their hopeful perception of their own possibilities). CHAR-5 impairs the recipient's hopeful perception by forcing them to see themselves through the contempt-er's false worth-assessment.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — CHAR-6 enables moral perception: the person with a clean conscience and blameless hands can perceive their own moral condition accurately (they know they are innocent) and can perceive God's response accurately (God confirms the innocent's claim, Gen 20:6). The loss of CHAR-6 impairs moral perception: Psa 73:13's crisis is a perceptive failure — the psalmist cannot perceive why innocent suffering exists; Hos 8:5's incapacity-for-innocence is a state in which the people cannot perceive their own moral condition accurately because it has been so long distorted by idolatry.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's perceptual engagement reveals a consistent bidirectional pattern: shame impairs horizontal perception (the humiliated cannot see their situation clearly; the contempt-shamed person cannot see their own worth accurately) while corrective shame can deepen vertical perception (Char 1 M07-C — shame before God enabling the person to see what God requires; Char 5 — divine reversal correcting the world's perceptual distortions). Every form of shame involves a distorted perception that needs correction. Haughty eyes (Char 2 — Isa 5:15; Psa 18:27) are the perceptive faculty's pride-distorted form; the seared conscience (Chars 1, 4) is the perceptive faculty's moral-distorted form; contempt (Char 5) is the perceptive faculty's worth-distorted form. The cluster's positive pole (Char 6) represents the perceptive faculty in its undistorted form — seeing one's moral condition accurately enough to claim innocence before God.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — CHAR-1 impairs the perceptive faculty selectively and severely. Psa 10:4 (vc=34074, M08-A2-VCG-02): "does not seek him; all his thoughts are, 'there is no God'" — total closure of the inner perceptive field to God; Isa 26:10 (vc=34024, M08-A4-VCG-05): "does not see the majesty of the Lord" — the specific perceptive capacity for divine majesty named as what is closed; Psa 10:5 (vc=34166, M08-A4-VCG-03): divine judgments are "out of his sight" — the proud person cannot perceive the standard by which they will be assessed. The impairment is directional: CHAR-1 does not impair all perception but specifically closes the perception of God, divine majesty, and divine judgment. It may enable a narrow self-centred perception — the proud person perceives themselves and their own achievement clearly — while systematically closing the broader perceptual field that would contextualise the self within God's reality.

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 impairs the perceptive faculty in the direction of divine authority specifically. Psa 86:14 (vc=34097, M08-B-VCG-02): God removed from the inner perceptive horizon. 2Pe 2:10 (vc=42739, M08-B-VCG-03): the self-willed "do not tremble before the glorious ones" — the perceptive faculty for spiritual authority (the capacity to perceive what is worthy of reverence) is closed. The impairment is directional: CHAR-2 closes perception of what should constrain the will, while the will's own purposes remain in clear focus.

**[CHAR-3]** E — CHAR-3 impairs the perceptive faculty for self-consistent moral assessment. Rom 2:23 (vc=33883, M08-C-VCG-01): the boaster in the law who breaks the law cannot perceive their own law-breaking, because the boast constructs a cognitive picture of the self as law-keeper that overrides the perceptive evidence of law-breaking. 1Ki 20:11 (vc=33353, M08-C-VCG-01): premature boasting impairs the perception of future uncertainty — the boaster "perceives" a victory not yet won.

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 impairs the perceptive faculty comprehensively in the direction of truth-about-self and truth-about-reality. 1Ti 6:4 (vc=33925, M08-D-VCG-02): "understanding nothing" — the most sweeping epistemic failure evidenced in M08. Col 2:18 (vc=33941, M08-D-VCG-01): inflation "without factual basis" — the perception of the self is divorced from actual evidence. CHAR-4 specifically impairs the faculty that would deliver accurate self-knowledge — the very perception that would correct the inflated self-picture is disabled by the inflation.

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-5 impairs the perceptive faculty for vulnerability and for God's power over structural strength. The ga.on proud-might of Egypt is consistently described as something that "will come down" (Eze 30:6, vc=33996; 30:18, vc=33997; 32:12, vc=33998) — but the nation with proud might does not perceive this coming reversal while it is strong. Lev 26:19 (vc=33982, M08-E-VCG-01): God "will break the pride of your power" — the power-holder does not perceive that their power is breakable until God breaks it. CHAR-5 enables the perception of one's own structural strength while closing the perception of its fragility before God.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All five characteristics impair the perceptive faculty, and all in the same directional mode: selective impairment of what would generate self-correction. The cluster comparison reveals that the impairment is self-sealing across all five — each characteristic closes the specific perceptive channel that would correct it. This is a cluster-level structural finding: M08 characteristics are self-sealing perceptively. What varies is which perceptive channel each characteristic specifically closes: CHAR-1 closes perception of God; CHAR-2 closes perception of divine authority; CHAR-3 closes perception of self-inconsistency; CHAR-4 closes perception of truth generally; CHAR-5 closes perception of vulnerability. The cluster's perceptive self-sealing explains the consistent pattern of requiring external catastrophic reversal for correction rather than self-initiated change.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Submission *enables and deepens* genuine reception of what is heard. Rom10:16 evidences that hearing without inner yielding is a deficient reception — the perceptive faculty hears but does not receive at the level required. Genuine submission enables the word heard to penetrate to the soul-level (1Pe1:22 — "obedience to the truth" purifying the soul). Conversely, the inner refusal that characterises non-submission (2Th3:14 — inner refusal revealed by failure to obey) impairs the perceptive reception of the authority's word — the person hears but closes against the claim. Submission thus enables the perceptive faculty's full function (hearing + yielding to what is heard) rather than its partial function (hearing + resisting).

**[CHAR-3]** E — Contrition *presupposes and deepens* the perceptive faculty. The characteristic cannot exist without a genuine inner perception of moral reality (the person must genuinely perceive their own failure or God's holiness). Conversely, the person whose perceptive faculty is distorted by pride or self-justification cannot arrive at genuine contrition — the blocking of genuine perception blocks the characteristic's formation. Contrition thus presupposes a functioning inner perception of moral reality and deepens it by validating the perception as accurate rather than allowing the self-protective deflection that would prevent it.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Meekness/gentleness *enables and deepens* genuine perception of others' conditions. The self-knowledge of shared weakness (Heb5:2) that grounds metriopatheō enables the person to perceive others' conditions with recognition rather than condemnation — the gentle person sees the erring through the lens of their own limitation and therefore perceives more accurately (without the distortion of assumed superiority). Conversely, the prideful assumption of superiority impairs genuine perception of the erring other's condition — severity replaces the perceptive empathy that shared-weakness awareness provides.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Semnotēs *enables accurate social perception* in others — the person of dignity is perceived clearly rather than through the distorting lens of ostentatious self-display or frivolousness. 1Ti3:4 — the orderly compliance the overseer's dignity produces implies children perceive the genuine authority-weight of the parent clearly. Tit2:7 — teaching authenticated by dignity enables hearers to perceive its content as genuinely weighty. The characteristic thus enables others' perceptive faculty to receive the person's authority and instruction without distortion.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Willing-heartedness *enables genuine reception* of the invitation to give. The freely-moved heart (Exo35:5/22) receives the call with openness rather than resistance — the perceptive faculty receives the call without the filtering of reluctance that the un-willing heart would impose. Psa51:12's request for a willing spirit implies that without it, the person cannot genuinely receive the possibility of joyful devotion — the burdened, not-yet-restored spirit perceives but cannot freely receive. Willing-heartedness thus enables the perceptive faculty to receive invitations to giving and service without the filtering of reluctance.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Humility *enables and deepens* the perceptive faculty. Pro11:2 — "with the humble is wisdom" — and the consistent pattern of God confirming he heard the humbling person (2Ki22:19; 2Ch34:27) together suggest that the humble person's inner receptivity allows genuine perception of divine address and of reality. By contrast, the non-humbling person (2Ch36:12 — Zedekiah) is evidenced as closed to the prophet's word — the perceptive faculty is impaired by the absence of humility. Col2:18 (the person puffed up by the "sensuous mind") shows that pride distorts rather than enables genuine perception. Humility, as the inner openness that does not close itself to external reality, actively enables the perceptive faculty to function without the distortion of self-referential protection.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All six characteristics enable and deepen the perceptive faculty; none impair it. The enabling mechanism differs by characteristic. CHAR-1 and CHAR-3 enable perception by removing the self-protective filter — the humble person (CHAR-1) and the contrite person (CHAR-3) are genuinely open to receiving reality because the self-enclosing distortion of pride has been lowered or broken. CHAR-4 enables perception of others by requiring genuine self-perception first — metriopatheō (Heb5:2) requires honest self-knowledge of one's own weakness before it enables accurate perception of the other's condition. CHAR-5 enables others' perception of the person — dignity removes the distorting noise of self-promotion so that the person is perceived clearly. CHAR-6 enables reception of invitations — the willing-hearted person receives the call to give without the filtering of reluctance. CHAR-2 enables full reception of the word heard — genuine submission enables the word to penetrate to the soul level (1Pe1:22) rather than being blocked by inner refusal. Cluster-level: M09 is a perception-enabling cluster — every characteristic in the cluster functions to remove the perceptive distortions that self-assertion produces.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — Wilful sinning *impairs* the perceptive faculty. The corpus evidence for the escalating pattern (Hos 4:7; 13:2 — "they sin more and more") implies a progressive desensitisation of the inner sense that registers God's presence and moral reality. Isa 1:4 ("they have despised the Holy One of Israel, they are utterly estranged") shows that sustained sinning produces estrangement — the inner perception of God as the moral reference point is diminished. Contrast with the deterrence register (VCG-03): where sinning is resisted, the perceptive faculty remains operative (Gen 39:9 — Joseph perceives the act as "great wickedness"; Exo 20:20 — fear of God "before you" enables perception). Sinning bypasses or progressively impairs the perceptive registration of God's holiness.

**[CHAR-10]** E — Enticement *captures and distorts* the perceptive faculty: 2Pe 2:14 — "eyes full of adultery" — the perceptive capacity has been turned into a desire-delivery mechanism; it no longer perceives neutrally but scans for what desire seeks. For hypocrisy (Gal 2:13) and apostasy (Act 21:21), the perceptive faculty's specific engagement is not evidenced in the corpus.

**[CHAR-11]** E — The condition *impairs and distorts* the perceptive faculty. Joh 16:8/9 — the world cannot self-perceive its sin-condition without the Spirit's external conviction; the perceptive faculty is blind to its own condition. Joh 9:41 — "you say, 'We see'" — the condition produces false perceptive certainty; the person under the condition perceives themselves as seeing clearly while the condition generates the blindness. Heb 3:13 — "deceitfulness of sin" — sin's deception operates through the perceptive channel, making the condition appear other than it is. Act 26:18 — "to open their eyes" — the gospel's work is a perceptive restoration that the condition has closed off.

**[CHAR-12]** E — Sin's enslaving power *impairs* the perceptive faculty: the enslaved person cannot accurately perceive their enslaved condition from within it. This is implicit in Joh 8:34 — Jesus declares the slavery to an audience that does not recognise themselves as slaves (Joh 8:33 — "we are offspring of Abraham and have never been enslaved to anyone" — the perceptive failure is the immediate context of Jesus's enslaving-power declaration). The enslaving power produces a perceptive blindness to the enslavement itself.

**[CHAR-13]** E — The record *distorts and eventually impairs* the perceptive faculty. Jer 16:10 — "they say to you, 'Why has the Lord pronounced all this great evil against us? What is our iniquity? What is the sin?'" — the people cannot perceive their own record even under judgment; the perceptive faculty is impaired by suppression of the conscience. Hos 12:8 — "in all my labors they cannot find in me iniquity or sin" — Ephraim's prosperity distorts perception of the record: wealth is mistaken for moral clearance. Conversely, when the record is made known (Lev 4:23 — "made known to him"), the perceptive faculty is restored to accurate moral self-assessment.

**[CHAR-14]** E — Forgiveness received *deepens* the perceptive faculty: Luk 7:47 — "he who is forgiven little, loves little" — the inverse implies that perceiving the magnitude of forgiveness received sharpens the person's perception of both their own moral condition and God's grace. The received forgiveness produces greater perceptive clarity about both the depth of the need (the many sins that were forgiven) and the depth of the gift (the love-response it generates).

**[CHAR-15]** E — The generational sinning pattern *impairs* the perceptive faculty's moral-spiritual interpretation function. Psa 78:32 — "despite his wonders, they did not believe" — the wonders are visually perceived but the generational pattern of unbelief impairs the perceptive faculty's capacity to process what is seen into trust. The pattern bypasses the faculty's normal function: ordinarily, evidence of God's power would produce faith; the generational sinning pattern insulates the community against this normal response.

**[CHAR-16]** E — The sinner-identity *impairs* the perceptive faculty in both the extreme-type sinner and the self-righteous observer. Amo 9:10 — "who say, 'Disaster shall not overtake or meet us'" — the habitual sinner's perceptive faculty fails to register the danger their identity creates; the perceptive capacity is impaired by self-deception. Joh 9:24 — the Pharisees' "we know that this man is a sinner" — the observer's perceptive faculty is impaired by prejudice: they perceive sinfulness where there is none (Jesus). Luk 13:2 — Jesus corrects the perceptive inference that suffering indicates greater sinfulness, revealing a general perceptive-faculty impairment in the population.

**[CHAR-17]** E — The guilt-state *activates and deepens* retrospective moral perception. Gen 42:21 — the brothers, under current distress, now perceive their past cruelty with moral clarity that they lacked in the moment; the guilt-state deepens perception of past events. Eze 9:9 — "they say, 'The Lord has forsaken the land, and the Lord does not see'" — conversely, extreme guilt produces a distorted perception: the guilt-burdened community misperceives God as absent; the accumulated guilt impairs accurate perception of God's continued presence and attention.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Iniquity *impairs* the perceptive faculty through its self-protective distortion mechanism. Psa 36:2 — the wicked person's self-flattery actively blocks accurate perception of his own iniquity; the iniquity distorts the very faculty that would perceive it. Hos 12:8 — Ephraim's wealth creates a perceptual blind spot; the accumulated iniquity is present (Hos 13:12 — "bound up") while perception sees nothing. Conversely, the conscience-engaged person's perception sharpens: 2Sa 24:10 — David's heart struck him — the perception of his own iniquity was immediate and accurate. Iniquity impairs perception when conscience is suppressed; it sharpens perception when conscience is engaged.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Transgression *impairs* the perceptive faculty in the sustained sinner. Isa 58:1 — "declare to my people their transgression" — the people cannot perceive their own transgression without external prophetic declaration; Isa 46:8 — "recall it to mind, you transgressors" — the transgressors' perceptive faculty has lost its grip on what they know. Psa 36:1 — "there is no fear of God before his eyes" — the eyes (perceptive faculty) are the seat of the replaced God-fear; transgression displaces what the eyes perceive. However, conscience-engaged recognition sharpens perception: Psa 51:3 — "I know my transgressions, and my sin is ever before me" — the penitent's perception is acute.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Unintentional sinning operates through the *bypassing* of the perceptive faculty — not by suppressing it but by the perceptive faculty not having the morally relevant input. Num 22:34 — Balaam's perception was not suppressed; the angel was simply invisible to him until disclosed. Lev 4:2 — the person's perception of the relevant prohibition was absent (through ignorance, not suppression). This is the critical distinction from CHAR-4 (Conscience suppression) and CHAR-1 (wilful sinning): in CHAR-2, the perceptive faculty is not overridden or bypassed by the will — it simply lacks the relevant information. The act occurs in the perceptive faculty's blind spot, not against its registered input.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Faithlessness *impairs* the perceptive faculty toward accurate self-assessment and *distorts* perception of God. 2Ch 12:2 — "because they had been unfaithful to the Lord, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem" — the people's unfaithfulness presumably preceded their recognising its consequences; the perceptive faculty failed to see the faithlessness until foreign invasion disclosed it. 2Ch 28:22 — Ahaz deepening in faithlessness under distress — the perceptive faculty fails to see faithlessness as the cause of the distress and instead deepens the response. Conversely: Ezr 9:4 — "those who trembled at the words of the God of Israel" — a functioning conscience-perception accurately registers others' faithlessness.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Perversion *blinds* the perceptive faculty. Exo 23:8 — bribery "blinds the clear-sighted" — the very clarity of the perceptive faculty is eliminated; Deu 16:19 — "blinds the eyes of the wise" — wisdom's perceptive capacity is impaired. Isa 29:16 — "you turn things upside down" — the perceptive faculty cannot correctly assess the creator-creature relationship; Jer 17:13 — those who "turn away from you" — the perversion of directional perception produces departure from God. Perversion blinds the inner perceptive faculty to both moral reality (what is right) and theological reality (who God is).

**[CHAR-22]** E — Injustice *impairs* the moral perceptive faculty in two directions. (1) *God-perception impaired*: Psa 53:1 — the heart's "no God" assertion impairs the fundamental theological perception; Job 18:21 — not knowing God is the perceptive deficit; (2) *Shame-perception eliminated*: Zep 3:5 — "the unjust knows no shame" — the conscience's perceptive-shame-response is absent in the established unjust person. The perceptive impairment is progressive: at the beginning the person may still perceive injustice (Job 34:32 — "if I have done iniquity, I will do it no more") but sustained injustice eliminates the shame-perception (Zep 3:5).

**[CHAR-3]** E — Genuine confession *deepens* the perceptive faculty: the act of naming sin precisely (Dan 9:5 — cascade of named failures; Num 21:7 — "for we have spoken against the Lord and against you") requires and reinforces accurate moral perception. The more specifically the sin is named, the more precisely the conscience's perception has operated. Hollow confession (VCG-03 — Deu 1:41; Exo 9:27/10:16 — Pharaoh) does not deepen the perceptive faculty — the words are produced but the perception does not shape the subsequent action of the will.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Conscience suppression *impairs* the perceptive faculty — specifically the inner moral-perceptive sense that should register one's own sin. Jer 16:10 (people fail to perceive their sin), Ecc 8:12 (sinner perceives repeated evil as unproblematic), 1Cor 15:34 ("drunken stupor" — a perceptive-alertness impairment). The impairment is self-reinforcing: the more the moral-perceptive sense is suppressed (through habituation, denial, or ignorance), the less capable it becomes of registering what it needs to register.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Refusal to repent *impairs* the perceptive faculty in its moral-gravity-assessment function: 1Ki 16:31 — the minimisation of the sin's gravity shows a perceptive faculty producing false assessments. Sustained refusal to repent (the Kings pattern across a lifetime — 2Ki 15:18) further impairs the perceptive faculty by habituating the person to perceiving the sinful course as normal and acceptable. The more consistently the turn is refused, the more the perceptive faculty adjusts to the sinful course as the default, making the gravity of the non-departure increasingly imperceptible.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Habitual defection *impairs* the perceptive faculty at its deepest level. 1Jo 3:6 — "never seen him or known him" — the impairment is not occasional but fundamental: the habitual sinner has *never* seen Christ, suggesting that the habitual sinning condition and the perceptive capacity for God are mutually exclusive. Ecc 7:26 — the sinner who is "taken" without escape — shows the perceptive faculty failing to detect the moral danger of the pattern before capture. The self-reinforcing mechanism (Hos 8:11 — altars for sinning producing more sinning) shows how the habitual pattern progressively impairs perception of the sinning course as problematic.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Contagious sin *bypasses* the perceptive faculty in the recipient community: the authority medium transmits the sinning direction through a channel that the community's perceptive faculty is designed to trust (the leader). Exo 23:33's snare imagery — and the preventive command — implies that the community will not perceive the contagious sin as a snare until they are already caught in it; the perceptive faculty is bypassed by the trust placed in the authority source. For the leader, the perceptive faculty is engaged in perceiving how to use authority to shape the community — but toward sinning rather than toward God.

**[CHAR-8]** S — The corpus does not evidence how the perceptive faculty is affected by political revolt. The 9 verses describe the political acts and their persistence without addressing whether revolt enables, deepens, or impairs the revolting party's perception.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Sinful speech *impairs* the perceptive faculty. 1Ti 6:4 — "understands nothing" combined with the slander that arises from it — the person who practises slander from conceit has a perceptive faculty that cannot accurately read reality. The more the conceit is sustained through slanderous speech (feeding on itself), the more the perceptive faculty is impaired. VCG-02's scribes — who see blasphemy where there is none — show a perceptive faculty that has been distorted by prior theological commitments so severely that it misidentifies the Son of God as a blasphemer.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Wickedness-as-settled-person-identity impairs the perceptive faculty. The evidence is consistent: Pro 4:19 (blindness to the cause of stumbling), Isa 26:10 (blindness to God's majesty), Dan 12:10 (inability to understand). The impairment is not merely incidental — it is described as constitutive of the wicked way: the darkness of the wicked person's way (Pro 4:19) is the condition from which their perceptive blindness flows. The characteristic does not enable or deepen perception. It bypasses moral-spiritual discernment in the sense that the wicked person acts without the check that clear moral perception would impose.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The characteristic impairs the perceptive faculty by constitutionally orienting it toward darkness. Mat 6:23 (vc=14458 — VCG-03) is the most direct statement: the bad eye produces darkness rather than light — the perceptive faculty no longer illuminates but obscures. Joh 3:19 (vc=14448 — VCG-04): the constitutionally evil person's works align their perceptive preference toward darkness — they prefer not to see the truth (Joh 7:7 — VCG-04: the world hates the one who testifies to evil works, because testimony forces perception of what the constitution prefers to ignore). The characteristic impairs perception specifically by orienting the whole inner person toward moral concealment and away from honest moral sight.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The characteristic impairs and bypasses the perceptive faculty in those who commit abomination. Isa 44:19 (vc=65961 — VCG-05): no discernment — the abominable inner condition has disabled the perceptive faculty of moral discernment. Pro 17:15 (vc=1690 — VCG-01): perverted judgment — the moral-perceptive faculty is not absent but inverted (justifying wrong, condemning right). In contrast, for those whose conscience is awakened, the characteristic deepens moral perception: Eze 9:4 (vc=1698 — VCG-04): those who grieve have a heightened perceptive sensitivity to the abominations around them. The characteristic's relationship to perception is thus dual: it impairs/bypasses perception in the abominable person and deepens it in those who grieve.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The characteristic enables and deepens the perceptive faculty in its misdirected form (toward idol-objects) while impairing it in its correctly directed form (toward God and moral reality). Eze 20:7-8 (VCG-05): the eyes actively feast on detestable things — the perceptive faculty is heightened in its idol-directed mode. Simultaneously, the characteristic impairs the moral-spiritual perceptive faculty: Eze 8:17 (vc=65980 — VCG-05): treating abomination as "too light a thing" shows that the moral-perceptive faculty cannot accurately assess the gravity of what is happening. The characteristic produces a perceptive split: enhanced idol-directed perception, diminished God-directed moral perception.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The characteristic impairs the perceptive faculty's moral-knowledge function (Psa 14:4; 53:4 — VCG-03: no knowledge in evildoers) while redirecting and enabling the surveillance-for-evil function (Isa 29:20 — VCG-02: "watch to do evil"). It also impairs the hearing faculty's responsiveness to moral instruction: Job 36:10 (vc=38215 — VCG-04): "He opens their ears to instruction and commands that they return from iniquity" — the need for divine ear-opening implies the characteristic has closed the inner ear to instruction. The characteristic thus produces a split in perceptive function: enhanced perception for opportunities to scheme harm, diminished perception of moral reality.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The characteristic impairs the perceptive faculty for moral-spiritual reality (Jude 10 — VCG-01: not understanding what they blaspheme) while leaving the physical perceptive faculty operational (Rev 16:9 — VCG-01: they know who has power over the plagues). The impairment is specifically moral-spiritual discernment — the capacity to perceive the value, authority, and holiness of what is blasphemed. The physical pain and heat are perceived but their spiritual significance is not: this is a spiritually selective perceptive impairment — physical pain is registered but its meaning (divine judgment calling for repentance) is not received.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster reveals a consistent impairment-pattern across all six characteristics for the moral-spiritual perceptive faculty: every form of M10b inner evil impairs the person's capacity to perceive moral reality accurately. Char 6 (Jude 10 — bypass: contempt fills the gap where understanding should be), Char 1 (Psa 10:4 — practical blindness to God), Char 3 (silenced conscience — Jer 6:15), Char 5 (Psa 14:4 — no knowledge among evildoers), Char 4 (Eze 8:17 — treating abomination as trivial). The exception is Char 4's visual-desire mechanism: the eyes' perceptive-desire faculty is heightened toward idol-objects while impaired toward spiritual reality. At cluster scope: M10b inner evil uniformly impairs moral-spiritual perception while sometimes redirecting perceptive capacity toward evil-enabling targets.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The characteristic enables and deepens perceptive faculty in the volitional/discernment register: sustained engagement with the clean/unclean categorical system trains the person in refined visual and categorical discernment (Lev 11:47: "to make a distinction between the unclean and the clean" — a cultivated perceptual discipline, M10c-B-VCG-01). However, the characteristic can also reveal the limits of perception: Lev 5:2-3 (M10c-A-VCG-01) shows that defilement can be acquired before the person perceives it — the condition precedes perceptual awareness, exposing the perceptive faculty's inadequacy to catch all contamination events. The conscience supplements what perception misses.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The characteristic impairs the perceptive faculty in its advanced form: Eph 4:19 (VCG-02) — "become callous" — the callousness of conscience includes a progressive impairment of the inner capacity to perceive moral reality correctly. The Tit 1:15 reference (VCG-03) — "to the defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure" — shows that advanced defilement produces a condition where the person's perceptive moral faculty cannot correctly assess moral reality: everything appears defiled because the instrument of perception (conscience, mind) is itself defiled. However, the characteristic also enables a negative form of perceptive sharpening in those resisting it: the positive-inverse (VCG-05 — Rev 3:4, 14:4) shows persons whose perceptive faculty has been maintained in moral clarity through not soiling their garments.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The characteristic impairs perception in two registers. (1) Self-perception: Jer 2:23 (VCG-02) — "how can you say, 'I am not unclean, I have not gone after the Baals'?" — the community cannot correctly perceive its own defilement-state; self-perception is compromised by the same self-deception that sustains the condition. (2) Priestly discernment: Eze 22:26 (VCG-05) — the priests' failure to teach clean/unclean distinction shows a systemic failure of the institutional perceptive-discernment faculty. However, the characteristic also enables a future acute perception: Eze 20:43 (VCG-02) — the community will "remember" and "loathe" — the eschatological perception of what they have done will be clear and grievous.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The characteristic impairs the perceptive faculty of the inhabited person: Mar 9:25 (VCG-01) — hearing suppressed; speech suppressed (the perceptive-expressive complex). The characteristic bypasses the person's perceptive self-awareness of their own condition — there is no evidence that the inhabited person perceives or articulates their own condition from within it.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's four characteristics form a gradient from perceptive deepening to perceptive suppression. Characteristic 1 deepens perceptive faculty: the purity system is a comprehensive training curriculum for visual and categorical discernment (Lev 11:47 — cultivating "the distinction between the unclean and the clean"). Characteristic 2 impairs the perceptive faculty in its advanced form: Tit 1:15 reference (VCG-03) — "nothing is pure to the defiled" — the perceptive-moral faculty can no longer correctly assess reality when the conscience is fully compromised. Characteristic 3 both impairs perception (Jer 2:23 — the community cannot perceive its own condition) and promises future restored perception (Eze 20:43 — the community will finally see clearly in the restoration). Characteristic 4 directly suppresses the perceptive faculty (Mar 9:25 — hearing suppressed). The gradient: deepening (Char 1) → advanced impairment through self-corruption (Char 2) → social-institutional failure with promised restoration (Char 3) → direct external suppression (Char 4).

The data implies two directional effects on perception, not previously assembled:

**Enables/deepens perception:** The woman of Luk 7:47 who has been forgiven much demonstrates a depth of perceptive orientation toward Jesus not shown by those who have not received forgiveness in the same way. The received forgiveness appears to sharpen the inner recognition of the forgiver's identity and worth — love much (the downstream inner state) implies a corresponding deepening of the perceptive orientation. Received forgiveness may recalibrate what the inner person is able to perceive and value.

**Blocks perception (when withheld):** The scribes' perceptive failure (Mar 2:7) occurs in the context of a presupposition — "who can forgive sins but God alone?" — that functions as a perceptive screen. Their theological framing prevents them from seeing the divine act occurring in their presence. The parallel: the unforgiving servant (Mat 18:35) who cannot perceive the incongruence of his own position (having received enormously and refusing to give a fraction) represents a kind of perceptive blindness — the inner inability to see one's own relational situation accurately.

*New finding:* The data implies that forgiveness received may **deepen spiritual perception**, while forgiveness withheld or misunderstood may **impair it**. This bidirectional effect on perception has not been assembled in existing observations and is worth flagging for Session D.

Enables and deepens. Zec 12:10: grace outpoured produces the capacity to see ("when they look on me, on him whom they have pierced") — grace enables the inner sight that recognises what grace has cost. SD012: grace enables hearing-receptivity. The impairment is in the counter-condition: pride and hardened hearing impair perception, and the absence of grace may sustain that impairment.

*Consistent with prior analysis. Adds faculty framing.*

Compassion both depends on and deepens perception in the verse evidence.

**Compassion depends on perception:** As established at Prompt 1, compassion cannot arise without the sight (or its inner equivalent) of the other's condition. It does not bypass the perceptive faculty — it is triggered by it. In this sense, compassion is perceptively dependent: blind to suffering, it cannot move.

**Compassion deepens perception — the neighbour question:** Luke 10:33-37 connects compassion directly to the capacity to see rightly. The question "who is my neighbour?" is answered by the parable of the Good Samaritan, whose compassion causes him to see the wounded man as someone worthy of full engagement. The priest and Levite also see (and pass by) — their failure is not perceptual absence but perceptual closure: they see without being moved. Compassion in the Samaritan deepens his perception to the point where the wounded stranger becomes a full person, not an obstacle. The priest and Levite's non-compassion leaves their perception impaired in the sense that it does not arrive at the full truth of what they are seeing.

**Compassion can be blocked by perceptive failure (eleeinos):** Where the person cannot perceive their own pitiable condition (Rev 3:17), compassion cannot reach them. Impaired inner perception blocks the reception of compassion. This is not compassion impairing perception — it is the absence of compassion's perceptive ground blocking its operation.

Contrition **deepens and sensitises** the perceptive faculty. The evidence from Isa 66:2 is that the contrite person trembles at God's word — a heightened inner responsiveness to divine speech that is specifically linked to the contrite posture. The one who is humble and contrite in spirit does not receive God's word with indifference or resistance; they receive it with trembling — a perceptive intensity that contrition enables.

The contrast is instructive: Jer 44:10 presents the people who have not walked in God's law — a failure of word-attentiveness. The hardened posture (absence of contrition) correlates with perceptive closure to God's word. Contrition, by contrast, opens and sensitises the inner perceptive faculty to divine speech.

*New finding: contrition functions as a sensitiser of the inner perceptive faculty, specifically with respect to God's word. The trembling-at-word in Isa 66:2 is not anxiety but heightened inner attentiveness — an acute responsiveness that the contrite posture enables and the hardened posture closes.*

**Enabling perception:** Genuine fellowship (righteous companionship, divine-nature participation) positions the person in community where their perception is extended — they have companions who will lift them up (Ecc 4:10), witnesses who have seen and heard and can share with them (1Jo 1:3). Fellowship is a perceptive amplifier in the righteous register: being rightly joined extends what the person can perceive.

**Impairing perception:** Idolatrous joining (Hos 4:17 — *Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone*) produces a condition of divine abandonment in which God's voice is no longer heard by the person. The wrong fellowship bonds impair the most crucial perception — receptivity to God.

**New finding:** Fellowship has a directly perceptive consequence that runs bidirectionally with the moral orientation of the fellowship object. Righteous fellowship opens perception; idolatrous fellowship closes it. This is not a marginal feature but a constitutive perceptive consequence of the fellowship bond.

Goodness deepens and enables the perceptive faculty. Psa 34:8 presents the encounter with divine goodness as sharpening inner perception — those who "take refuge" and "taste" develop a refined capacity to recognise what is genuinely good. The comparative wisdom mode (884-004) requires and develops discernment — the better-than sayings train the evaluative perception to distinguish inner goods from lesser goods. Conversely, the absence or distortion of goodness impairs perception: Mal 2:17 / Jer 44:17 name the inversion of the moral perception faculty as the condition where evil is called good. This implies that goodness-present sharpens perception; goodness-absent or distorted corrupts it. The perceptive faculty and the goodness-characteristic are mutually reinforcing: genuine goodness cultivates perception; accurate perception recognises genuine goodness. (OBS-067-OBS-025, OBS-067-OBS-021, SBF-067-Q065)

Love primarily **enables and deepens** the perceptive faculty. It enables: love for God opens the person to perceive what others cannot — Hos 6:6 (OBS-103-091) pairs knowledge of God with chesed, implying love as the condition for spiritual perception of God's ways. Love deepens: Phili 4:8 (OBS-103-133) — the mind directed to attend to what is lovely (prosfilēs) — love sharpens the inner sense for what is worth perceiving. Joh 15:15 (OBS-103-052): Jesus' love-disclosure opens the disciples' perception to what he has heard from the Father. Conversely, disordered love **impairs** perception: Luk 16:14 (OBS-103-136) — the Pharisees' love-of-money produces rejection of what they hear; Joh 3:19 (OBS-103-147) — love of darkness blinds to the light. The direction of love determines whether the perceptive faculty is opened or closed.

The evidence shows both enabling and impairing: Genuine mercy enables relational perception (seeing the face — Gen 32:20; access to divine presence — Exo 25:22 from SD014). Corrupted mercy (*kopher* as bribe) impairs moral perception (blinds eyes — 1Sa 12:3, OBS-111-044). The impairing effect appears in the corruption of mercy's mechanism — when mercy-vocabulary is applied to injustice, it destroys the very perception that mercy should enable. OBS-111-040, OBS-111-044.

Contrition deepens perceptive capacity in one specific direction: it opens the person to receive divine address (trembling at God's word — Isa 66:2). The contrite person is not closed to divine communication but particularly open to it. The hardened alternative (Jer 44:10 — not walking in God's law) implies perceptive closure to divine word. *New finding: contrition deepens the perceptive capacity for divine address — the contrite person is specifically receptive to God's word in a way the hardened person is not.* OBS-030-060, OBS-030-028.

Fellowship enables perception in two directions: it enables accurate perception of the fellowship object's nature (2Cor 6:14 — the call to discern light from darkness), and inverted fellowship impairs perception — Hos 4:17 presents Ephraim "joined to idols" as a condition in which the joining itself has disabled exit. Habitual wrong-fellowship may progressively impair the perception needed to recognise the error. OBS-062-042, OBS-062-049.

Forgiveness deepens and opens perception — specifically perception of divine character. Psa 130:4 (forgiveness encountered → reverential fear produced) implies that the encounter with forgiveness as a divine quality sharpens perception of who God is. The Pharisee's limited love (Luk 7:47 — "forgiven little, loves little") implies limited perception of the magnitude of the forgiveness — perception of the gift's magnitude determines the love-response. OBS-064-020, OBS-064-029.

Covenant engagement enables and deepens perception; covenant breach impairs it. For enabling: Psa 25:14 — God makes known his covenant to those who fear him; the covenant-keeping person receives deeper discernment of God's reality and purposes. The new covenant explicitly promises restored perception: "they shall all know me" (Jer 31:34) — the new covenant produces a knowing that is itself a form of deep inner perception of God. For impairing: 2 Cor 3:14 — "their minds were hardened... a veil remains" (OBS-034-072). The old covenant read without Christ impairs cognitive-perceptive engagement; the veil blocks what was meant to be seen and known. Covenant-breaking also impairs — Jer 11:8 frames covenant breach as failure to incline the ear: the breaking of the covenantal relationship is accompanied by a closing of the perceptive faculty.

Peace enables perception — specifically, the silence/stillness dimension of peace enables the perception of the divine voice and divine reality. The pattern: demamah (profound silence, H1827) is the threshold before divine speech (1Ki 19:12, Job 4:16 — prior session OBS-117-069, 070); the quieted soul is receptive; the restless soul cannot hear what silence carries. Conversely, the absence of peace impairs perception — "failing eyes" (Deu 28:65) is the somatic expression. The mechanism: peace as stillness creates the condition for perception; restlessness as noise prevents it. This is the hearing-direction of the silence vocabulary: peace enables the person to be still enough to perceive God.

Receiving divine inner-being giving enables perception in two ways. (1) The Spirit-giving (Neh 9:20) produces the capacity to receive instruction — the Spirit opens the inner ear/mind to formative input. The giving of Spirit is itself a perceptive-enabling gift. (2) The failure to give glory to God (Jer 13:16, OBS-060-047) impairs perception: "while you look for light he turns it into gloom." The non-giving of glory produces perceptive disorder — the light-seeking faculty encounters only darkness. These together show the characteristic enabling perception when received rightly and impairing it when the relational correspondence breaks down (failure to give glory). The Spirit-endowment is the most direct perceptive-enabling instance.
